text:
In the third year, after all the visions given to the prophet Daniel, the angel Gabriel, who had previously been sent to him, was sent by the Lord. He said to him: ‘Daniel, man greatly desired, I have been sent by the Lord to you to speak words to you and to show you the end of the days that are to come after the coming of the Word which I proclaim through you.’

A virgin will be in Israel, and she will receive the Word from the Word; this one will become human for the sake of the world and will bring many from Israel to life. Pay close attention and hear what is about to happen at the end of the days in all cities and lands because of human wrongdoing. I, Daniel, said: ‘Speak, my lord.’ After he had finished all the prophetic words concerning all the cities and lands, he spoke of Asia, Pontus, Phrygia, Galatia, Cappadocia, Carpathia, Smyrna, Antioch, Alexandria, Egypt, Nicaea, Nicomedia, Carthage, Byzantium, Babylon, and Rome.

The tears of the sons and the spread of famine will ruin the fruitful earth. Your rulers will become sons of lamentation, and all your possessions around you will be doomed to destruction and carried away from you to Babylon of the Seven Hills.

The ruler of Pontus will fall, and the sword will destroy his sons. His warriors will fall by the sword’s edge; most will be taken to Byzantium and buried there.

The children of the Phrygians will perish for lack of bread. Their land will be cracked by drought, and they will become food for the birds; many of them will flee to Carthage.

Fire will appear from heaven in Galatia, and thunder and lightning will destroy it. The thrones of its rulers will fall to the ground; its southern side will be burned with blood and fire, and many will then flee to Rome.

In Lesser Cappadocia its children will kill and capture one another. Its rulers will be defeated, and those around it will be in hardship and lamentation in Lesser Babylon.

In Carpathia its children will suffer affliction. They will see fires but will not believe. The earth will split, all will reach hell, and many will flee to the Seven-Hilled City.

In Smyrna wrath will increase and become like a cup full of blood, and a fall from on high will take place. Your rulers will be removed and your nobility will fall, for the day of the Lord’s wrath will be upon you.

The children of Antioch will perish, its raised buildings will collapse, and its rulers will not enjoy them. There will be a shaking within you, and the abundance of your kingdom’s wealth will destroy you.

Many disturbances of war will take place in Alexandria, and the uprising will reach the archers of its fortresses. Its rulers will be pursued.

The sons of Egypt will flee, struck by famine. Your possessions will be destroyed, the Nile will dry up, and your rulers will perish.

The daughters of Nicaea will be in mourning and distress because their relatives and husbands have been taken captive by the strong; your rulers will become servants of people they do not know.

Woe to you, Nicomedia, which lifted up your horn and consumed the bodies of the holy ones who were in you! You will be handed over to destruction through the blood of righteous people, who will repay you what is due; you will sink as far as hell. Weep and lament, wretched one, for you will be destroyed with your children. Your rulers are rulers of sighing, your priests love gold and silver, and the beauty of your splendor will sink.

Carthage and the people of Persia: you do not know what will happen to you at the end of the days, nor how long a span you will be granted at the end of eternity, after all the cities and lands. You will perish from famine, city adorned with gold and silver, people decked out and ornamented! Licentiousness will be strong in you; your children will play with gold and then perish from famine.

The land of Byzantium and Babylon will sink, seized by the strong; their foundations will be ruined and their power will fall.

There will be no ruler in Rome at that time, yet its sword will be sharpened, its arrow strong, and its cunning increased. A ruler will rise and fall repeatedly. It will have three roads. Many will fear you because of the pomp of your many rulers, your proud neck, and your great wealth.

The children of Byzantium will appear with wondrous power, for a man from Byzantium will go from Byzantium to the so-called Seven-Hilled City and lay its foundation. His name will be known among all the inhabitants of the world, through the diversity of languages. A wonder-worker will rebuild it, born of a devout woman. In his time the desire of his heart will be fulfilled; he will find the Tree of Life, and his staff will be great. He will find the nails that were in that sign and put them into his bridle to win frequent wars. His horn will be high and strong, his name among all languages, and the city will be given an everlasting remembrance.

And after him the third scepter will rise, shedding the blood of righteous men. He will proclaim commandments but will not know God; he will touch the holy writings with a blinded heart. After him a man who loves wisdom will come to you, Babylon of the Seven Hills, and set up an image within you, because of which you will not be violated. After all these things, higher horns and greater scepters will arise; they will be strong over you, and their memory will be very great.

Another scepter is also exalted. It will become wondrously strong and be lifted up because of the Lord’s name and proclamation, for God’s gift was in him. Through him there will be great life, and all people will rejoice in delight in him. They will gather to you from cities and lands, arriving in you, the Seven-Hilled City, and each will perform his work. The scepter of kingship will be strong until its end comes.

From one scepter two scepters will emerge: one of your scepters will be a wild beast, and the second a beast on both roads of the Seven-Hilled City. From Rome fierce wrath will come upon you, swollen like a full cup, until your time arrives. At one time the city’s art of song will be your good; at another, your wealth will be a spring for all. You will be adorned like a bride and appear like a widow. Your rich clusters, as they once were, will diminish; your great glory will be divided and sink.

The kingdom within you will raise up another scepter called Theodosius. He will be holy, and his name will be sanctified in you, O Seven-Hilled City. At his birth your children will rejoice, and each will do as he thinks. All cities and lands will serve you; in your abundance the earth will be rich in splendor. The Nile of Egypt will water you, and you will become the wall of the churches. Fear and trembling will be great under his scepter; this will be the beginning of sighing in your kingdom, and the time of his rule will be long and strong. His scepter will conquer to the ends of the whole earth, from east and west, from north and south. His neck will be firm, his right hand strong, and his years many, as happened to no other king. After all this he will turn his face toward his father; his years will be many, his name fearsome, and his kingdom exceedingly glorious.

A third king will be under you in Rome, the Seven-Hilled City. You are called Seven-Hilled because the whole people of Persia will enter you, O Rome; they will not rule until the end of eternity. As a second ruler, an old man named Marcianus will reign in you. His scepter will last for less time than the first, and his rule will be exceedingly dreadful. That time will be good for some and bad for others. His kingship will last for times, times, and half a time, granted to him by your Builder, O Seven-Hilled City. Through the writing of faith he will exalt himself. Great division will break out under his rule: priests will fall from their seats, many cities will be destroyed, and people will undergo many changes, but your beauty and extent, O Seven-Hilled City, will not diminish. After all this he too will go to his fathers.

Another scepter will rule in you. It will be a wild beast and will take up the first scepter, which will one day be struck by the dog. This wild beast

will be as great and strong as the first in speech and wisdom, and he will not reject his nobility. His neck will be like a calf’s neck and his eyes like a lion’s eyes. He will roar terribly, and all cities and lands will tremble before his horns. In his time a rainbow will appear in the sky, and various signs in heaven and on earth. The sound of thunder and the fall of many cities will be heard; the earth will split and buildings will fall from their foundations. His roads will be fiery, and wars will be in him and in you, Seven-Hilled City. Then your glorious buildings will be burned by fire and your heights leveled to the ground. Your sons will lament in you; your great joy will turn to mourning, and your sons will drag the corpses of the great across the earth.

Suddenly a storm will come from heaven and cover the earth. Dragon-shaped peoples will appear on earth. Many will become poor and many poor people rich, and great confusion will be in you. Cry out, warriors of Thrace and Cilicia, with weapons and sword! At that time the wild beast will send his sword eastward but will not prevail. A man whose body above the loins is shaped like a dragon will mock him. He will send his second sword westward, but will not defeat him there either; the dog will mock the dragon.

The dog will press the wild beast with many gifts, gold, and money. The dog will rebel against the wild beast and cause his young to ascend the throne of the wild beast and the scepters. The dog will destroy the wild beast, its snares will be taken away, and the dogs will cast the wild beast out. Everyone will see the dog chasing the lion. The lion will return and kill the dog and its young. The lion will roar exceedingly powerfully; his roar will be heard in all cities and lands, and fear of him will be in his snares,

and people will be confused by the lion’s roar and by the dog’s death.

The second dog will pursue, changing its tongue, as far as the lion’s snare; it will withdraw from him if it cannot harm him. The dog’s cub will hide for times, a time, and an hour; in its own time it will rule. Its name will be ‘the dog’s cub,’ meaning ‘scepter of the peoples.’ The wild beast will utterly erase the dog’s memory. They will knowingly sing false accusations against him; in his city they will destroy his image. Many trapped by the wild beast will think to kill him, but they will not succeed. His co-rulers will be killed by the sword in another city, and the priest’s petitions concerning the Unknown will be recognized.

One of the great men, a young man among the wild beast’s warriors, will bind the feet and hands of many and send them to the wild beast. Then, when the wild beast summons many people from different nations to serve him as a lord, another man will appear before him and take him into his bosom. He will pursue the warriors, and they will pursue him; he will flee from them on foot, and no one will catch him because he is swift on foot. He will flee to the wild beast and to the one in his bosom and enter to him. The little wild beast will come out boldly, and the great wild beast will set him on his throne and make him his co-ruler and fellow-sitter instead of himself: two wild beasts dwelling in one cave. The young one will boldly prepare for war, while the great beast will return to the land from which he came.

The young beast will take his place for a time, appointed king by no one but gaining the snares of kingship by his own power. The young beast will go to the great beast, leaving his snares to their maker; it will conquer you, Seven-Hilled City, and hold you in distress. Its joy will be great; it will be merry, loved by the Great One and hated by many. It will grant life and wealth, and the dragon will play with it and lead it with the wild beast’s hunting staff.

Woe to you in that time, Babylon of the Seven Hills, when the widow rules, the dragon pursues the foreigner, and the foreigner called Salamander turns to flee. If he turns his face toward the islands, the gold, silver, precious stones, and crown of the scepters, and the one in the wild beast’s bosom—tripled from the people of Persia in Carthage—none of the people will pursue him, because they love the dragon and the great splendor that was in you. He will wander from land to land, tormented by foreign peoples. When he is tormented by them in care and on the road [the German edition marks “road” as uncertain], he will sigh to his Creator together with his innocent ones.

The hunter’s staff, which belonged to the wild beast, will join the dog. The dragon will hold the place of torment and ceremony, following after its empty thrones and pursuing the holy place. He will rebuke the dragon with his tongue on account of the righteous and the relics of the saints. He will abolish the leadership of the patriarchs and lead the church of the sanctuary into captivity. Those who live in clefts, caves, and caverns of the earth, wandering in the wilderness, will come to you, Seven-Hilled City, violated by the dragon. After all this they will shake the dust of their feet over you, bearing witness against you. Then the beauty of your splendor will be burned with fire, and a young man will flee, pretending that he is bringing the first scepter, called Salamander, with his hunting staff.

At that time the dragon will be in distress, captured by his followers and bound by those on the left, and no one will receive him because he has shed the blood of the saints

in the cities and lands. He will flee into the holy temple which he had earlier taken captive, but no one will receive him, for heavenly blows will be upon him. The young man will come to Salamander and bring the foreigner before the dragon [the German editor notes an uncertain Armenian reading here]. When the dragon sees him, he will flee from him. The foreigner will not kill the dragon but drive him from his presence. The young man will fall with a great fall, and the widow will not escape. They will show him the foreigner and his co-ruler, and they will pay tribute in the booths of the one who created him. On his throne the blood of his father will be demanded, and the foreigner will become great in a short time.

There will be abundance in you, Seven-Hilled City, and many deaths among the people who have gathered to you from the cities and lands. Earthquakes will occur in many places. Many will hear a voice and not believe. Your wealth and splendor have darkened you, because you are proud and arrogant; your extravagance has brought you low, yet abundance and beauty will still be great in you. The end of time will come upon you, and from you the hunter’s staff that comes from the dragon will depart. People will go to the lands of foreigners. Your daughters will adorn themselves to tempt young men and ruin many; your great men will fall, and there will be much fear and confusion.

Then a death-dealing angel will strike you together with all the cities and lands, and violent deaths will be sent from heaven. Suddenly he will be angry with the earth; the earth will quake, temples will fall, and their houses will become graves. The sea will raise its waves high and cover the people, though some will flee and be saved. Then a gathering of angels will appear before the throne and make a plea. Then you, Babylon of the Seven Hills, will weep for your children, putting on sackcloth and scattering ashes on your head, when you see people dying for their sins and crimes. Men and children, women and infants will perish because the Lord’s anger is upon them.

Your protective walls will burst and your booths will be leveled to the earth. Nursing children with burned mouths will cry out to God; your priests will scratch themselves as they mourn your scepters. Your great men will weep, your fellow citizens will be wholly sorrowful, and your travelers will be in distress. Your grapes will fall, your vineyards will be destroyed, and the earth will crack with a crash, giving people over to destruction, even nursing infants and the aged.

Yet God will not destroy you completely, Seven-Hilled City, because the time of your destruction has not yet come. He will not shut the people in the abyss, because your time has not yet come. Torments have been prepared for you, because you have committed every injustice within yourself, taking the earth into your bosom. The thoughts of people will be greatly confused until the Lord commands from above that people be destroyed. The Lord’s decree will appear, showing where the punishment is to take place, and those who took refuge in you will receive torments.

The people who hoped in you and the hunter’s staff will destroy you. The cub will pursue the other cub, demanding the blood of its fathers; it will willingly hand itself over to the foreigner, to the dogs and their helpers. It will bring forth languages and peoples and rule many nations. The two dogs will fight one another and destroy each other.

Woe, when the widow rules and craftily attacks the foreigners, while another foreigner seeks her destruction and destroys her by deceit! Those days will be dreadful and evil. The children of the scepters will be confused, fighting among themselves. Great distress and evil will then befall people, such as never was before. The ruler will not trust Salamander, for he is a foreigner. His people will receive what they did not seek. Salamander will want to flee but will be unable; he will be caught, and Plakitas will kill him.

Another scepter will rule in you, Seven-Hilled City, and there will be many birth pangs. A poor man will arise who knows no kindness: arrogant, proud, loving gold, eager for battle. His name is Orloyios. His throne will last only a few days; he will be angry, his great men will hate him, and his fellow citizens will be tormented by him. Heavenly wrath will be in his days, and he will repeatedly oppress Babylon. During his rule the voice of a messenger of disaster will come to you, and the warriors of the barbarians will trouble you, though they will not fight.

Another tyrannical king will rise against him and pursue him in battle. With much grief and lamentation he will take his life. This one will rule and seize the scepter that is in you, Seven-Hilled City; he will become great on high and splendid thrones, a man valiant to the left and right. In his time there will be a great famine, not a small one; the earth will be corrupted by people, waves of water will flow, and the air will be pitch-dark and murky. Your vineyards will diminish, your beauty will be afflicted, the days will be shortened, and the day will last six hours.

Woe to the people who will be alive at that time! The king will turn his face toward the west. Then woe to you, Seven-Hilled City, if your king is a young man! Great distress will befall you at that time. A man will take his brother’s wife, a son his mother, a daughter will enter her father’s bed, and a brother will take his sister,

and there will be blasphemies, murders, perjuries, slanders, lies, profanations, torments, plunderings, hatred between brothers, and disturbances. The consecrated servants will be slaughtered in the temple. Kings will attack kings and rulers attack rulers; the powerful will fall upon the poor, and both rich and poor will fall.

Bithynia, which lies on the seashore, will be leveled by earthquakes. The waves of the sea will rise and cover the foundations of Bithynia as far as the little city of Nicomedia.

Then another king will arise. His time will be few days, evil and exceedingly dreadful; from then on there will never again be a good time, only evil. His son will fight with him and destroy him with the sword.

Another king will come from another religion: Arianos. He will draw everyone to himself. Woe to you, Seven-Hilled City, at that time, for you will mourn yourself and your boundaries more than all others!

Then kings, rulers, leaders, and champions will fall over cities, lands, and places. There will be many uprisings and disturbances among the people. The barbarian people will attack cities and lands, and the earth will sink seventy-three cubits under the multitude of peoples. Then they will not oppress you, Seven-Hilled City; only war will torment you. The ease of life in you will diminish, wrath from heaven will be upon you, and great blows will strike you. A pillar of fire will appear on earth, descending from heaven. Then your rule will change, and you will remain desolate from disease and famine. The second scepter will then be split apart and carried to another city by an insignificant ruler. Fiery arrows will rain from heaven, and there will be many signs and wonders.

Then the Antichrist will rule, and people will turn away from the service of God to unbelief, following the coming of the one they neither wanted nor hoped for, because they did not believe in him, who stood against everything.

The one they did not want will be conceived and born from a defiled virgin, and the scepter of deceit will rule humankind. For three times and a half he will bring many souls to ruin, so that they become heirs together in eternal hell. Then the angels will be confounded when they see the signs he displayed earlier. When God-fearing people hear of him, they will know and see the adversary of all humankind. These are his signs: his joints are inflexible; his eyes are diseased; his eyebrows are smooth; his fingers crooked; his head pointed. He is handsome, boastful, wise, sweet-smiling, visionary, clever, intelligent, gentle, calm, and a worker of wonders. The souls of the lost are near him. He makes bread from stones, opens the eyes of the blind, makes the lame walk, and moves mountains from place to place. He will perform all these things in appearance, and many will believe in him. Woe to those who believe in him and accept his signs! Their right hands will be bound so that they cannot return to the one in whom they had hoped before.

Then there will be a great famine. Heaven will send no rain, the earth will grow nothing green, and all fruits will wither. All cities and lands will mourn for themselves. People will flee, but they will not be able to flee from east to west or from west to east. Only those living on mountains, in caves, clefts, and caverns of the earth will be able to flee, until the second coming of the one born of the holy Virgin. Then his chosen ones will be known, as they see the Lord’s everlasting coming. He will be represented, many will be judged, and there will be storms from heaven. Then a terrible tribulation will be in the universe. Woe to pregnant women and nursing mothers in the last days! Woe to the unrestrained, who have believed in the adversary

and worshiped him, and to those who accepted everything revealed about his coming!

After all this has happened, and after the inspired and righteous people have suffered, afflicted by distress and violence, the end will finally come. Some people will recognize the Seven-Hilled City by the signs that have been given and will say: ‘Was there ever such a city?’ A woman will walk across the earth from east and west, north and south, and find no fruit except an olive tree. She will embrace the olive tree, sigh, and say: ‘Happy is the one who planted this olive tree!’ Her spirit will rise up from her at that very moment.

Then the sun will turn to darkness and the moon to blood; the stars will fall like leaves, and the sky will be rolled up like a scroll. The sea will foam up from its depths and overflow to cover the people; everything will be burned and dried up by the air. Fiery angels will descend from heaven, and fire will blaze through the universe. Fiery, bronze-colored mice and similar creatures will appear; flesh-eating beasts will come out of the mountains. The one who was not sought will not be afraid. The land of the ungodly will be destroyed, and the righteous will be received by the Father, because a command has come from the Lord.

The thrones will fall, the books will be opened, and courts will be set up. The angels will blow their trumpets, and the righteous will gather in a dance, offering songs of praise to the Father. They will be judged according to their deeds; the Lord alone is the righteous judge, and all his works are righteous. All human generations will open their mouths and cry: ‘Lord, Lord, do not lead us into temptation, but deliver us from evil, for you know and understand that we cannot endure it, since we are flesh. But as a loving and kind Father, have mercy on us, for yours is the glory, now and always, from eternity to eternity. Amen.’
